pk.context: 200 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A phenyltriazine antiepileptic whose half-life runs from about 13 to 70 hours depending on co-medication, with a boxed rash warning.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is 98%, with negligible first-pass metabolism, and food has no effect. About 55% is bound to plasma proteins, and it is cleared mainly by glucuronic acid conjugation.
Molecular weight 256.09. Very slightly soluble in water, 0.17 mg/mL at 25°C, with a pKa of 5.7.
Approved under an NDA as scored tablets of 25, 100, 150 and 200 mg, and also as tablets for oral suspension and orally disintegrating tablets.
Boxed warning for serious skin rashes, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, that can need hospitalization. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity; nausea, insomnia and somnolence are common.
Epilepsy: adjunctive therapy for partial-onset, generalized tonic-clonic and Lennox-Gastaut seizures from age 2, and conversion to monotherapy from age 16.
Its precise mechanism is unknown. A phenyltriazine chemically unrelated to other antiepileptics, it prevented seizure spread in maximal electroshock tests in animals.
The generic name begins with L and has eleven letters.
